why.Genesis 1:1: 'In the beginning' — the biblical claim that the universe had a start. The Kalam argues for the same start.
why.Romans 1:20: Paul's warrant for arguing from the world to God at all. It is why a case like this exists.
why.Hebrews 11:3: Says what is seen was not made from what is visible. The nearest biblical echo of a cause outside matter.

why.Psalm 19:1: 'The heavens declare the glory of God.' The oldest form of the argument from the sky.
why.Isaiah 45:18: God formed the earth 'not to be empty' but to be lived in. A claim that the setup is aimed at life.
why.Romans 1:20: Paul's licence for reasoning from what is made. The verse standing behind all these arguments.

why.Romans 2:14-15: Quoted in the case. People without the law 'do by nature what the law requires'. It blocks the slur.
why.Micah 6:8: 'Do justice, love mercy.' A moral demand stated as something already known, not argued for.
why.Psalm 97:2: Justice is 'the foundation of his throne' — the claim that the Good is God's own nature, not his decree.

why.Genesis 1:27: People made in God's image. The claim that mind sits at the base of things, not at the end of a chain.
why.John 1:1-4: Reason itself, the Word, is placed at the start of everything. The passage this argument echoes.
why.Proverbs 20:12: 'The hearing ear and the seeing eye' — God made them both. Cited for senses built to know.

why.1 Corinthians 15:3-8: Paul's list of appearances. It is the earliest written source for the facts this case is built on.
why.Mark 16:1-8: Cuts both ways. The women do find the tomb, but the earliest text ends with no appearance at all.
why.Acts 2:22-32: Peter preaching the resurrection in Jerusalem itself. It is where the early-preaching fact comes from.
why.Galatians 1:18-19: Paul meets Peter and James three years on. The link to both conversions, in Paul's own hand.

why.1 Corinthians 15:3-8: The creed itself. Paul says he 'received' and 'delivered' it, which marks it as older than his letter.
why.Galatians 1:18-19: Paul's own dating. He meets Peter and James in Jerusalem three years after he changed sides.
why.Luke 24:34: 'The Lord has risen and appeared to Simon' — a second, separate trace of the same early formula.

why.1 Corinthians 15:6-8: The group appearances, including 'more than five hundred at once'. A hallucination is private by nature.
why.John 7:5: 'Not even his brothers were believing in him.' It sets up how odd James's later role is.
why.Acts 9:1-9: Cuts both ways. Paul was hunting Christians, not grieving. But the account reads as light and a voice.
why.Mark 3:21: His family thought he had lost his mind. The other half of the case that James was no follower.

why.Luke 1:1-4: Luke says he checked with eyewitnesses and wrote an orderly account. That is the claim being tested.
why.2 Peter 3:15-16: Calls Paul's letters 'scriptures' already. A sign they were copied and shared very early.

why.Isaiah 40:8: 'The word of our God endures forever.' The scrolls put that claim to a thousand-year test.
why.Jeremiah 36:1-4: Jeremiah dictating to Baruch, who writes it on a scroll. A picture of how these texts were made.

why.2 Peter 3:15-16: Already calls Paul's letters 'scriptures'. A collection existed long before any council met.
why.Luke 1:1-4: Luke names his method: eyewitnesses, careful checking, an orderly account. One of the later tests.
why.Colossians 4:16: Paul tells one church to swap letters with another. That swapping is how a collection begins.

why.2 Kings 19:32-36: The siege that ends without the city falling. Sennacherib's own prism claims no capture either.
why.2 Kings 20:20: The one-line note about Hezekiah's waterworks. The tunnel is still there to walk through.
why.Ezra 1:1-4: Cyrus sending exiles home to rebuild. The Cyrus Cylinder sets out that same Persian policy.
why.2 Samuel 7:16: The promise of a lasting house for David. The Tel Dan stone names that house on an enemy's monument.

why.John 5:2: The pool with five colonnades. Long called a mistake, until diggers found exactly that layout.
why.John 9:7: The Pool of Siloam. It was uncovered in 2004, during a sewer repair.
why.Matthew 26:57: Names Caiaphas as high priest. A bone-box found in 1990 reads 'Joseph son of Caiaphas'.
why.Luke 3:1: Luke's dated list of rulers, Pilate among them. The Caesarea stone gives Pilate his right title.

why.Luke 2:1-7: The verse with the problem. It dates the birth to a census 'when Quirinius was governor of Syria'.
why.Matthew 2:1: Puts the birth under Herod the Great, who died in 4 BC. The other half of the collision.
why.Acts 5:37: Luke himself mentions the census and the revolt that followed. He knows the AD 6 event.

why.Ezekiel 26:3-14: The oracle against Tyre. Many nations, broken walls, rubble scraped into the sea, a bare rock.
why.Ezekiel 29:17-20: The self-correction. Nebuchadnezzar 'got no wages' from Tyre. The case says lead with this one.
why.Isaiah 13:19-22: The doom on Babylon. It did come, but over centuries. Do not compress the timeline.
why.Jeremiah 51:37: Babylon to become heaps and a waste. The same picture, and the same caution applies.

why.Daniel 7:13-14: The 'son of man' figure. Older than Jesus on either date, and the point the case says to use.
why.Daniel 9:24-27: The seventy-weeks timetable. It is also older than Jesus, on either date.
why.Daniel 11:31-35: Cuts against you. This is the chapter whose precision, then failure, is the dating fingerprint.
why.Daniel 5:29-30: Belshazzar ruling in Babylon. The book knows a fact that later Greek writers lost.

why.Isaiah 52:13-53:12: The servant passage. The Great Isaiah Scroll carries all of it, dated to about 125 BC.
why.Psalm 22:1-18: The lament with the mockery, the divided garments and the lots. Verse 16 is textually disputed.
why.Luke 24:25-27: Jesus reading the whole of Scripture as about himself. The root of the Christian reading.
why.Acts 8:32-35: The Ethiopian reads Isaiah 53 and asks who it means. The earliest recorded use of the passage.

why.Job 38:1-7: God's answer to Job is a presence, not an explanation. The case says that is the biblical reply.
why.Romans 8:18-25: Creation groaning, with a glory still to come. The Christian frame for pain that is not yet explained.
why.John 11:35: 'Jesus wept' at a grave he was about to open. A response, not an argument.
why.Revelation 21:4: 'He will wipe every tear.' A promise that it ends. The sceptic notes that is not the same as a reason.

why.Isaiah 45:15: 'Truly, you are a God who hides himself.' Scripture grants the very thing the objection names.
why.Jeremiah 29:13: 'You will find me when you seek me with all your heart.' The promise the honest seeker says failed.
why.Psalm 13:1-2: 'How long will you hide your face from me?' The Bible's own lament at this silence.
why.Matthew 11:25-27: Things hidden from the wise and shown to children. Cited for a God who is not evenly obvious.

why.Deuteronomy 20:16-18: Cited by the objection, not against it. As written, it commands total killing. The hardest text here.
why.Genesis 15:16: 'The sin of the Amorites is not yet complete.' Cited for a long delay before judgement.
why.Exodus 23:29-30: 'Little by little I will drive them out.' The Bible's own softer verb, on a slow timescale.
why.Judges 1:27-33: Peoples said to be wiped out are still there, in numbers. Evidence the earlier wording is overstated.

why.Psalm 90:2: 'From everlasting to everlasting you are God.' God does not begin, which is what the question assumes.
why.Exodus 3:14: 'I AM' — God named as sheer being. The old basis for calling him necessary rather than caused.
why.John 8:58: 'Before Abraham was, I am.' The same claim, and now on the lips of Jesus.

why.Genesis 1:1-2:3: The creation account itself. Note that days one to three come before the sun is made.
why.Psalm 104: A second creation poem, plainly poetry. Scripture tells this story in more than one way.
why.Job 38-39: God's tour of the natural world, in verse. Nobody has ever read it as a mechanism.
why.2 Peter 3:8: 'A day is with the Lord as a thousand years.' Used for day-age readings, though its subject is patience.

why.Jeremiah 17:9: 'The heart is treacherous.' Quoted in the case as the doctrine the war figures fit.
why.James 4:1-2: 'What causes wars among you? Your cravings.' The Bible names appetite, not creed, as the driver.
why.Matthew 26:52: 'All who take the sword will perish by it.' Jesus disarming one of his own men.
why.Romans 3:10-18: 'None is righteous, no, not one.' The claim that the problem is human, not tribal.

why.Psalm 19:1-4: The wonder itself is biblical. But this is testimony, not an argument you can win with.
why.Romans 1:20: Paul's claim that God is perceived through what he made. It backs fine-tuning, not the banana.

why.Proverbs 18:17: The first to plead seems right until another examines him. Both claims fail that examining.
why.1 Thessalonians 5:21: 'Test all things.' The rule that should have caught these two before anyone repeated them.

why.Exodus 20:16: 'Do not bear false witness.' Quoted in the case. There is no exemption for apologetics.
why.Ephesians 4:25: 'Put away falsehood; speak the truth.' The same command, aimed at the church itself.

why.Deuteronomy 6:5: 'Love the LORD your God with all your heart.' The call a fire-insurance bet cannot produce.
why.Jeremiah 29:13: 'Seek me with all your heart.' Seeking, not betting. That is Pascal's real prescription.
why.Hebrews 11:6: Says God rewards those who seek him, but also that one must first believe he is. Awkward for a bet.

why.Romans 2:14-15: Serves the sceptic here. People without the law 'do by nature what the law requires'.
why.1 Peter 3:15-16: Answer 'with mildness and deep respect'. The standard all three of these lines break.
why.Proverbs 18:13: Answering before you have heard the matter is folly. That is what mind-reading a person is.

why.Acts 12:1-2: The one apostle whose death the New Testament records. Herod had James put to the sword.
why.1 Corinthians 15:14-19: Paul says that if Christ was not raised, their preaching is empty and they are false witnesses.
why.2 Corinthians 11:23-28: Paul's own list of what the claim cost him: beatings, prison, shipwreck. First-hand, not legend.
why.Acts 26:9-11: Paul describing how hard he once hunted Christians. It is why his change of side counts.

why.Acts 12:1-2: The only apostolic death in the New Testament. One, not twelve. That is the whole correction.
why.1 Thessalonians 5:21: 'Test all things.' A rule that would have stopped this claim before it spread.
why.Proverbs 12:22: 'Lying lips are detestable to the LORD.' Why an overclaim is not a small thing.
